note: Re-judged 2026-11-03 by an independent auditor who authored none of 816ce1ce4c, 2cbd255ba4, 2e5c2d012a, d22b811ce4 or 1a2ccaeef8 (phase 5 of spec-filter-wire-0-umbrella, the per-peer text filter chain deleted). Draft Section 6 read: "If the Next Hop field is malformed, the implementation MUST handle the malformed UPDATE message using the approach of "treat-as- withdraw", as described in section 7.3 of [RFC7606]." The only moved unit, TestRFC2545EffectivePairPolicyAndMixedSibling, changed only its export-filter plumbing: The test filter is now an answerTransport behind filterTransportSeam, compiled by answerPolicy into a policychain library chain, so the verdict travels the real filter-update path (route.Input, rpc.FilterUpdateOutput decoded by the library chain) instead of the deleted policyFilterSeam that handed a PolicyResponse straight to the text chain; that is the production path every plugin filter now takes. The filter is now called once per UPDATE and rewrites only when the fields carry the IPv6 prefix 2001:db8:7::/64, where it was called per family on the text. The tagged negative row cap77-source-invalid-second-withdrawn has no replacement, installs no policy, and still returns through rfc2545AssertWithdrawnAtReceipt, which requires the Session to publish the withdrawal of every route of the UPDATE, legacy sibling included, and no announcement to the recipient; every assertion is byte-identical. The other carriers of the row are unmoved and their judgement stands. Ran the tagged units under ./le job run at HEAD (-tags ze_bgp, -v): PASS (scratch audit-p5-units-v.log). Verdict unchanged: enforced.
